subject: Operational evidence: VM scan index, patch roadmap & SLA exception request
messages:
From: Ethan R. <ethan@topline-audit.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
Cc: security@brightline.io
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: consolidated VM scan index + patch roadmap for SIG

Hi Lauren,

As part of the SIG / CAIQ intake for Brightline's SOC 2 readiness, we need a consolidated index of vulnerability scans and an operational patch roadmap covering the past 90 days. Specifically:

- Master index that references each scan (tool, date, scope, S3/Drive link).
- Current patch backlog snapshot grouped by severity + assigned owner and ETA.
- Any SLA exceptions for critical CVEs (if remediation window exceeded).

Brightline's security team asked for an export they can attach to the SIG questionnaire; can you provide the index and a short note describing scan cadence and remediation SLAs? If there are exceptions, please attach the exception request PDF or the ticket link.

Thanks — Ethan
Ethan R.
Senior Auditor, Topline Audit

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
To: Ethan R. <ethan@topline-audit.com>, security@brightline.io
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.example.com, monica_patel@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated VM scan index + patch roadmap for SIG

Ethan —

We're attaching an index and a patch backlog snapshot below. Quick summary for the SIG intake:

- Scan cadence: authenticated full-stack scans weekly (FortifyScan + open-source credentialed scanner), lightweight host-level quick scans nightly for triage.
- Coverage: prod and staging clusters (all VPCs) + external perimeter; third-party libs scanned weekly via SCA pipeline.
- Remediation SLAs (target): Critical (CVE score >=9.0): 72 hours; High (7.0-8.9): 30 days; Medium: 90 days (exceptions allowed with documented approval).
- Evidence links: s3://redwood-vm-evidence/2027/05/index.csv (attached and mirrored in Drive).

Note: We have one active SLA exception for CVE-2027-1144 (third-party dependency requiring vendor patch) — request PDF attached.

Attachments: redwood_vm_scan_index_20270511.csv; patch_backlog_snapshot_20270510.csv; sla-exception-request-20270512.pdf

Let me know if you need a condensed single-page statement for the SIG questionnaire.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com

From: markus_klein@redwood.example.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com, Ethan R. <ethan@topline-audit.com>, security@brightline.io
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.example.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated VM scan index + patch roadmap for SIG

Quick operational note — adding context for the patch backlog CSV:

- The CSV includes a column "remediation_wave" which maps to our weekly patch windows (Tue night for infra, Thu morning for app teams).
- For CVE-2027-1144: vendor acknowledgement received 2027-05-09; estimated vendor patch ETA 2027-06-14. We've opened a patch escrow plan and scheduled mitigations (WAF rule + rate-limit) in place.
- For all open Criticals we maintain a Kanban swimlane and a daily 09:00 stand for ownership coordination.

If Topline wants an isolated spreadsheet with only SIG-relevant fields (evidence artifact IDs + hash + immutable timestamps) we can produce that.

-Markus
Principal, Vulnerability Management
Redwood Inference

From: Ethan R. <ethan@topline-audit.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com, markus_klein@redwood.example.com
Cc: security@brightline.io
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 13:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated VM scan index + patch roadmap for SIG

Thanks Lauren/Markus — this looks good. Two follow ups:

1) Can you confirm whether the weekly authenticated scans include credentialed container image scanning (SCA) as part of the same job or as a separate pipeline? We note separate SCA artifacts in the backlog.
2) For the SLA exception PDF, can you confirm the approval chain and whether Brightline needs a separate signature from your VP of Engineering to accept the exception for their SIG filing?

If you can answer those, we can close this evidence request and attach it to the SOC/SIG packet.

-Ethan

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
To: Ethan R. <ethan@topline-audit.com>, security@brightline.io
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.example.com, monica_patel@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: consolidated VM scan index + patch roadmap for SIG

Ethan —

Answers below and final confirmation:

1) Scan composition: weekly authenticated "full-stack" run orchestrates three steps: credentialed host scan (NessusEnterprise), container image SCA (Clair-based SCA job), and dependency SCA in CI (Snyk/OSS pipeline). Artifacts for each step are referenced in the index CSV under "artifact_id". We ran the integrated job on 2027-05-04 and 2027-05-11; both artifacts are present in the index.

2) SLA exception approval: the exception PDF includes required approvers — Security Director (my signature) and VP Engineering approval is optional for internal policy but Brightline has requested VP sign-off. I've looped in Marissa (VP Eng) on this message. Marissa — can you sign the attached exception or confirm you approve Brightline to accept the exception as-is for their SIG submission?

If Marissa confirms, Topline/Ethan can close the evidence request and mark the exception as "approved for audit". Happy to provide a one-page narrative mapping these artifacts to the SIG question IDs if you'd like.

Thanks,
Lauren

Attachments: sla-exception-request-20270512.pdf (signed by Security Director)
